title: File organiser with --dry-run
prompt:
Write organise.py so that `python3 organise.py [--dry-run] SRC DEST` sorts the files in SRC into DEST by the date in their file name:
- Recognised date forms: YYYYMMDD, YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY.MM.DD and YYYY_MM_DD (the same separator throughout), not part of a longer run of digits. The first recognised date that is a real calendar date with a year from 1990 to 2099 wins; if there is none, the file is undated.
- A dated file moves to DEST/YYYY/MM/<same name>; an undated file moves to DEST/unsorted/<same name>.
- Never overwrite: if the target exists, use name-1.ext, name-2.ext, ... (the first free one).
- Only regular files directly inside SRC; skip subdirectories and names starting with '.'.
- Print one line per file, in name order: "move SRC_PATH -> DEST_PATH". With --dry-run, print the same lines but change nothing on disk.
- Running it again when SRC has nothing left to move changes nothing.
Sample files are in inbox/. Use only the Python standard library.
